reviewer.scope: same-provider editorial review only; not different-provider release acceptance

findings: Casablanca option discussion included Ingrid Bergman, who is not a candidate, and omitted Cary Grant, who is.
The two musical-theatre articles used the literal Russian term 'книга' where 'либретто (сцены и диалоги)' is clearer.
Learning interpretations needed to be explicitly labelled as interpretations rather than sourced historical facts.

items.evidence: AFI credits Garland as Dorothy Gale. The Shirley Temple note remains factual, and the inner-route wording is now explicitly a learning association.

AFI credits Bogart as Rick Blaine, Henreid as Victor Laszlo and Rains as Louis Renault. The revised text accurately distinguishes those two candidate distractors from non-candidate Ingrid Bergman and candidate Cary Grant.
MTI credits Sondheim for music and lyrics and James Lapine for the book. The Russian article now explains the latter as 'либретто, то есть сцены и диалоги' and labels its learning lens.
MTI credits Sondheim for music and lyrics and George Furth for the book. The Russian article now uses the same libretto clarification and labels the interpretive reading as a learning device.

known_out_of_scope_follow_up.finding: The authoritative public Casablanca stem needs the Russian accusative 'кто сыграл Рика Блейна?'. It is a canonical-question follow-up and was not changed in this article-only review.
